comments.why_zh: 由 4KB 可执行文件实时生成的 demo 与臃肿形成对比。
comments.quote_zh: 建议看看这个由 4KB 可执行文件实时生成的 demo
comments.text_zh: 那些看不出一个 8KB+ 的可执行文件除了退出并返回一个值之外什么都不做有什么不寻常或浪费之处的人，建议看看这个由 4KB 可执行文件实时生成的 demo：[VIDEO] 这里还有更多：[LINK] demoscene 基本上与主流软件文化完全相反，虽然它聚焦于多媒体表演，但我认为他们的一些技术和底层动机可以更普遍地应用……我在想，最简形式的 /bin/true 和 /bin/false 是否甚至达到了可受版权保护的最低“创造性要求”，以及它显著膨胀的原因是否正是为了满足这一点。
comments.text: Those who don't see anything unusual or wasteful about an 8KB+ executable whose only action is to exit and return a value are recommended to watch this demo generated in realtime by a 4KB executable: [VIDEO] There's more here: [LINK] The demoscene is basically the exact opposite of mainstream software culture, and although it's focused on multimedia shows, I think some of their techniques and underlying motivation could be applied more generally... I wonder if /bin/true and /bin/false in their most simplest forms even meet the minimum "requirement for creativity" to be copyrightable, and if the reason why it has bloated significantly is so that it could be.

comments.author: david-given
comments.story_title: Voxel Quest Fluid Dynamics and New Rendering Method
comments.quote_zh: 创作了许多惊艳的 demo
comments.text_zh: 数学并不难，但你确实需要较好地掌握向量以及（可选地）3D 变换矩阵，而且在搞懂术语之前它相当晦涩。我自己没做过 GPU raymarching，但我在 CPU 侧用过同样的技术来开发一个整颗行星的程序化渲染器（当然是用 Ada）；raymarching 相对直接，但我在尝试让体积大气效果正常工作时严重卡住了。我发现一个非常有用的资源是 Iñigo Quilez 的网站；特别是他那篇关于基础地形 raymarching 的文章解释了大部分概念：[LINK]（他也叫 iq，创作了许多惊艳的 demo，包括 4kB demo _Elevated_：[VIDEO] 他似乎还写了 ShaderToy。搜索 iq 就能看到他的作品。omfg，ShaderToy 现在能让你编写 shader 来生成 _音乐_ 了？[LINK]）
comments.text: The maths isn't hard, but you do need a decent grasp of vectors and (optionally) 3D transformation matrices, and it's pretty opaque until you figure out the terminology. I haven't done GPU raymarching myself but I've used the same techniques on the CPU side in order to develop a whole-planet procedural renderer (in Ada, of course); the raymarching was relatively straightforward but I got horribly bogged down trying to make a volumetric atmosphere work. One resource I found really useful was Iñigo Quilez' website; in particular, his article on basic terrain raymarching explains most of the concepts: [LINK] (Also known as iq, he's responsible for a number of amazing demos, including the 4kB demo _Elevated_: [VIDEO] He also appears to have written ShaderToy. Search for iq to see his stuff omfg ShaderToy lets you write shaders to produce _music_ now? [LINK] )

comments.author: userbinator
comments.why_zh: 一个 4096 字节可执行文件实时生成的视听 demo。
comments.quote_zh: 你看到和听到的一切都由一个 4096 字节的可执行文件实时生成
comments.text_zh: 这些大小对比也很有用，至少能说明即便是简单的“非 Modern”C++ 程序也已经有不少膨胀。编译耗时 0.064 秒，生成 8480 字节的可执行文件。我熟悉汇编，所以能凭直觉做出数量级估算，但即便是不熟悉的人，也应该试着大致估算实现那段代码需要多少机器指令，并得出结论：三个嵌套循环里没多少东西，再加一次比较、一些算术运算和少量库函数调用，却要超过 8000 字节，这似乎相当过分。就连 800 字节都偏高了——我的估计大概在 100 到 200 字节左右。另外，看看这个 4K demo（你看到和听到的一切都由一个 4096 字节的可执行文件实时生成）：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The size comparisons are also very useful, if anything to show that even the simple "non-Modern" C++ program already has quite a bit of bloat. Compilation takes 0.064 seconds, produces 8480 byte executable I am experienced with Asm so I can come up with an instinctive order-of-magnitude estimate, but even those who aren't should try to roughly estimate how many machine instructions are required to implement that code, and come to the conclusion that over 8000 bytes for three nested loops with not much in them, a comparison, some arithmetic, and a handful of library function calls seems rather excessive. Even 800 would be on the high side --- somewhere around 100-200 bytes is my estimate. Also, watch this 4k demo (everything you see and hear is generated in realtime by a 4096-byte executable): [VIDEO]

comments.author: zxcdw
comments.why_zh: 这个 demo 比一个基本图标还小。
comments.quote_zh: 所含字节数比一个基本的 32 位 32x32 像素图标还少
comments.text_zh: 这是那个人观点的一个绝佳例子：[LINK] 那是 128 字节。你可以把它编码成一张 43 像素的 RGB888 图像。这比 7x7 像素图标还小！正如 Jare 在另一条评论中提到的，这个视频 [VIDEO] 所含字节数比一个基本的 32 位 32x32 像素图标还少。demoscene 这整件事的某些精髓，就是在这些限制（256 字节、1024 字节、4096 字节、64 kbytes……）内创作出这类艺术。自定义虚拟机、即时解压算法和方法、精心构造的数据以及巧妙的数据复用方式才是关键。这就像黑魔法。
comments.text: This is a great example of the point the guy is making: [LINK] That's 128 bytes. You could encode that as a 43 pixel RGB888 image. That's less than 7x7 pixel icon! Now as Jare mentioned in another comment, this video [VIDEO] contains less bytes than a basic 32-bit 32x32 pixel icon. Some of the whole essence of this demoscene stuff is to work within these constraints(256 bytes, 1024 bytes, 4096 bytes, 64 kbytes, ...) to produce this kind of art . Custom virtual machines, on-fly decompression algorithms and methods, carefully crafted data and ingenious ways of data re-use are the key. It's like black magic.

comments.author: userbinator
comments.story_title: Reducing the size of iOS app binaries
comments.why_zh: 在不到 4096 字节内运行时生成内容的例子。
comments.text_zh: 把那种“雪花噪点感”的背景换成纯灰色后，载荷大小降到了约 20M，省了约 30Mb。我知道事后看来这有点显而易见，但你本可以保留类似原始背景的东西，同时通过运行时生成它来大幅减小体积——生成一个看起来随机的背景的代码可能只有几十个字节，而且对多种分辨率可以通用。想看更多这种技术的例子，可以看看 demoscene 作品——下面这个视频是由一个不到 4096 字节的二进制文件生成的：[VIDEO] 源码：[LINK] 说明：[LINK]
comments.text: Switching out of the "staticy" background for a plain gray reduced the payload size to ~20M, a savings of ~30Mb. I know this might sound somewhat obvious in retrospect, but you could've retained something similar to the original background and reduced the size significantly by generating it at runtime --- the code to create a random-looking background may only be not more than a few dozen bytes, and can be the same for multiple resolutions. For more examples of this technique, see demoscene productions --- the following video was generated by a binary of less than 4096 bytes : [VIDEO] Source code: [LINK] Explanation: [LINK]

comments.author: userbinator
comments.why_zh: 可与飞行模拟讨论相提并论的 4 KB demo。
comments.text_zh: 这让我想起这个 4 KB demo：[VIDEO]（源代码和讨论见 [LINK]；说明见 [LINK]）。不过从技术角度看，那个飞行模拟更有意思一些，因为它是可交互的，而且没有用 GPU 来完成大部分计算。另外，尽管源代码被混淆了，但注意那些仍然可见的“外部符号”，例如 XDrawLine、XSetForeground 等，已经能相当好地概括它是如何做事的——一般来说，在逆向工程或分析软件时，检查“黑盒”与外部世界交互的地方，是理解它的重要一环。
comments.text: I am reminded of this 4 kilobyte demo: [VIDEO] (Source code and discussion at [LINK] ; explanation at [LINK] ) although the flight sim is a little more interesting from a technical perspective, since it's interactive and also not using the GPU to do most of the computation. Also, despite the source code being obfuscated, observe that that "external symbols" which are still visible, e.g. XDrawLine, XSetForeground, etc. already give a pretty good overview of how it does what it does --- and in general, when reverse-engineering or analysing software, inspecting where the "black box" interacts with the rest of the world is an important part of understanding it.
